note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Lung nodule found on imaging.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents after incidental finding of lung nodule on chest imaging. Patient initially presented to PCP with a cough and was diagnosed with bronchitis. PCP ordered a chest x-ray to rule out pneumonia, which revealed a lung nodule. CT scan subsequently confirmed the nodule. Patient reports having an on-and-off cough for approximately three months, first noticed when loading hay bales with horses (approximately 400 bales per day). Patient then developed a cold, which prompted visit to PCP. Patient exercises regularly with biking and typically does not get sick. Cough has resolved. Patient expresses nervousness about the finding.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies pain or shortness of breath.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis (fair control, remains stable without recent flares). Former smoker, quit approximately 7 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. No family history of lung cancer. No family history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Former smoker who quit 7 years ago and reports feeling better after cessation. Actively exercises, primarily biking on trails. Has horses.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 16, O2 sat 98% on room air, afebrile.
Lungs: Clear and equal bilateral.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no clicks, rubs, or murmurs, no extra beats.
Extremities: Skin pink, warm, and dry. No edema to lower extremities. Swelling noted to knuckles on third digit bilaterally. Pulses intact in all extremities. Capillary refill brisk.

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 cm smooth nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. No emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule. Will order pulmonary function tests for baseline lung function assessment. Will schedule PET CT to determine if nodule is metabolically active. Will perform video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery with three small incisions to right chest, general anesthesia, approximately 1.5 hours duration. Post-procedure chest tube to be removed the following day. Hospital admission for one night. Removal recommended given smoking history, though nodule could be benign. Continue rheumatology follow-up and continue current methotrexate therapy.
